Subject: Audit logs & export formats — follow-up from discovery call

Hi Sofia / Tim,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clear breakdown of FinCo's audit/evidence requirements. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align engineering work: 

- Requirements we heard: ability to produce per-request access logs showing who accessed customer data (user_id / actor identity, actor_email, timestamp, object_id, action (read/export/delete), IP, and any applied masks).
- Desired export formats: CSV for SOC upload, and S3/JSONL for programmatic ingestion into your archival system.
- Retention ask: SOC/Compliance wants evidence up to 7 years for certain datasets; we discussed possibility of an export/archival workflow versus keeping raw event logs live.

Can you confirm the exact fields your audit team needs (if anything beyond the list above) and whether you need sample exports with synthetic data for an initial review? Also, are there any redaction/hashing requirements for PII in the exported files (e.g., hash emails vs plain text)?

Next steps I propose from our side: we prepare a sample CSV export (synthetic data), provide a short doc describing default retention windows and options for extended retention, and schedule a 30-min follow-up tech call with our infra lead to demonstrate an export and answer scope questions.

If that works, I can loop in our infra lead (Aditya) and our solutions engineer (Marissa) for the follow-up.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the recap — that'll work. A few clarifications from our side:

- Required fields: actor_email, actor_role (service/user), actor_id, timestamp (UTC), action, object_id (document/session id), object_type, ip_address, result (success/fail), and a correlation_id.
- Export format: CSV is preferred for legal reviews, JSONL for ingestion. We also prefer exports that can be uploaded to our S3-bucket (we can provide a write-only presigned URL).
- PII: For GDPR purposes we need to know if raw message content or any free-text user content appears in the logs. Ideally logs should not contain message bodies; if any user-identifiable content is present, we need a redacted version (emails hashed using SHA256 or similar).
- Retention: Our baseline request for audit evidence is 7 years for privileged access events. We understand that's long; please state your standard/available retention options.

For the SOC review this week we need a synthetic CSV sample with the above fields and a short statement on retention policy and redaction options. Can you deliver that by Tue 3/3? If not, let us know the earliest date.

Thanks,
Sofia Martinez
Director, Information Security
FinCo Bank

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a synthetic sample CSV and a short playbook that outlines our default retention windows and options for extended retention/export. High-level answers below; details are in the attachments.

Attachments:
- audit-logs-export-sample.csv (synthetic data; header row includes: timestamp_utc, actor_email, actor_role, actor_id, action, object_id, object_type, ip_address, result, correlation_id)
- redwood-audit-logs-playbook.pdf (retention options, export mechanisms, redaction config)

Quick answers to your questions:
- Message bodies: Redwood's audit logs do NOT include full message bodies or user-submitted content. Logs capture metadata about accesses and events only (actor identifiers, object ids, action types, timestamps, IPs).
- PII/Email addresses in logs: By default actor_email appears in logs to support customer audits. We support configurable redaction/hashing on export; options include SHA256 hashing of email addresses or tokenization. Exports can be run with redaction enabled.
- Retention windows: default detailed event retention is 365 days. For customers requiring longer retention for audit/compliance we provide two options: (1) long-term archival export to customer-controlled S3 (we can automate exports daily/weekly) and (2) extended retention add-on (up to 7 years) as an enterprise feature with associated storage fees and SLA.
- Export formats: CSV, JSONL are supported. We can also stream logs into customer-owned S3 or push to a secure FTP endpoint.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you prefer redacted exports (hashed emails) or plain exports for SOC ingestion.
2) If you want long-term retention via S3, share the upload mechanism (presigned S3 write URL or target bucket details).
3) I'd propose a 30-min technical demo to show the export flow and redaction settings — are you available Wed 3/4 or Thu 3/5?

If the sample looks good, we can produce a full export of the last 12 months of events (synthetic for the trial) and provide instructions for automating exports to your archive.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
